content: 1. When clarithromycin is co-administered with drugs that prolong the QT interval, close monitoring of the ECG is recommended to prevent potential cardiac complications. 2. Clarithromycin increases the plasma levels of letermovir by inhibiting its metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely when these drugs are used together. 3. Co-administration of letermovir, a substrate of OATP1B1/3, with OATP1B1/3 inhibitors may lead to increased plasma concentrations of letermovir. Monitor for potential adverse effects. 4. Leuprolide increases the toxicity of clarithromycin by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely due to the increased risk of torsades de pointes. 5. Both clarithromycin and levalbuterol prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely to mitigate the risk of arrhythmias. 6. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of levamlodipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. 7. Co-administration of amlodipine with moderate or strong CYP3A inhibitors increases systemic exposure to amlodipine, potentially necessitating dose reduction. Monitor for symptoms of hypotension and edema to determine if dose adjustment is required. 8. Both clarithromycin and levofloxacin prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 9. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of levoketoconazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of levomilnacipran by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. Do not exceed 80 mg/day of levomilnacipran when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 11. Clarithromycin decreases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 12. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase plasma hormone concentrations. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 13. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of loperamide by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Clarithromycin increases the levels of lumacaftor/ivacaftor by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. However, due to the induction effect of lumacaftor on CYP3A, the net exposure of ivacaftor at steady state is not expected to exceed that of ivacaftor monotherapy. No dose adjustment is necessary when CYP3A inhibitors are initiated in patients already taking lumacaftor/ivacaftor. When initiating lumacaftor/ivacaftor in patients taking strong CYP3A inhibitors, reduce the dose to one tablet daily for the first week to allow for the steady-state induction effect of lumacaftor. After this period, continue with the recommended daily dose. No dose adjustment is required for moderate or weak CYP3A4 inhibitors. 15. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of lumateperone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. Limit the dose to 5 mg/day when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 16. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of maraviroc by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Reduce the maraviroc dose to 150 mg BID when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 17. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of marijuana by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of mavorixafor by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Both mavorixafor and clarithromycin prolong the QTc interval. Monitor QTc during treatment in patients with risk factors for QTc prolongation, such as co-administered medications that increase mavorixafor exposure or other drugs with a high risk of QTc prolongation. 19. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Clarithromycin decreases the levels or effects of mestranol by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low. 21. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of mestranol by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Both clarithromycin and methadone prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 23. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of methylprednisolone by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 24. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of mifepristone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. Do not exceed 300 mg/day of mifepristone for Cushing syndrome when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. The combination may also prolong the QT interval. Use alternatives if available. 25. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of mirvetuximab soravtansine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase exposure to unconjugated DM4, the cytotoxic component of mirvetuximab soravtansine, potentially increasing the risk of adverse reactions. 26. Mitotane decreases the levels of clarithromycin by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Mitotane is a strong inducer of CYP3A4; monitor for possible dosage adjustments when co-administered with CYP3A4 substrates. 27. Clarithromycin increases the toxicity of momelotinib by inhibiting OATP1B1/B3 transporters, leading to increased plasma concentrations of momelotinib. Use caution and monitor closely for adverse reactions. 28. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of mometasone (inhaled or intranasal) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely, as this may increase the risk of systemic corticosteroid side effects. 29. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of montelukast by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Clarithromycin increases the levels of naldemedine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely for potential adverse effects. 31. Clarithromycin decreases the levels of nateglinide by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely, as this may result in hypoglycemia. Monitor glucose levels closely. 32. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of nelfinavir by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of neomycin (oral) by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of netupitant/palonosetron by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Netupitant is primarily metabolized by CYP3A4; no dosage adjustment is required. 35. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of nicardipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely, as increased effects of calcium channel blockers may lead to hypotension, edema, decreased heart rate, and acute kidney injury due to reduced renal blood flow. 36. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of nifedipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Consider initiating nifedipine at the lowest dose available if given concomitantly with clarithromycin. 37. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of nilotinib by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 38. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of nimodipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely, as increased effects of calcium channel blockers may lead to hypotension, edema, decreased heart rate, and acute kidney injury due to reduced renal blood flow. 39. Clarithromycin increases the levels of nintedanib by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. If adverse effects occur, management may require interruption, dose reduction, or discontinuation of therapy. 40. Nirmatrelvir increases the levels or effects of clarithromycin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. Do not exceed clarithromycin doses >1,000 mg/day in patients taking protease inhibitors. Consider dose reduction in patients with renal impairment. 41. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of nisoldipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely, as increased effects of calcium channel blockers may lead to hypotension, edema, decreased heart rate, and acute kidney injury due to reduced renal blood flow. 42. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of nitrendipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 43. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of norgestrel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic concentrations of norgestrel, potentially increasing the risk of adverse effects. 44. Both clarithromycin and ofloxacin prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 45. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of oliceridine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. If concomitant use is necessary, less frequent oliceridine dosing may be required. Monitor closely for respiratory depression and sedation, and titrate subsequent doses accordingly. If the inhibitor is discontinued, consider increasing oliceridine dosage until stable drug effects are achieved. Monitor for signs of opioid withdrawal. 46. Both clarithromycin and olodaterol (inhaled) prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely, as drugs that prolong the QTc interval may potentiate the cardiovascular effects of beta-2 agonists, increasing the risk of ventricular arrhythmias. 47. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of osilodrostat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Both osilodrostat and clarithromycin prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 48. Both clarithromycin and osimertinib prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Conduct periodic monitoring with ECGs and electrolytes in patients taking drugs known to prolong the QTc interval. 49. Clarithromycin increases the levels of ospemifene by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 50. Oxaliplatin increases the levels or effects of clarithromycin through other mechanisms. Use caution and monitor closely. Monitor for ECG changes if therapy is initiated in patients taking drugs known to prolong the QT interval. 51. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of oxybutynin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 52. Both clarithromycin and ozanimod prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Due to potential additive effects on heart rate, treatment with ozanimod should generally not be initiated in patients concurrently treated with QT-prolonging drugs with known arrhythmogenic properties. 53. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of paclitaxel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 54. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of paliperidone by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Both clarithromycin and paliperidone prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 55. Clarithromycin increases the levels of panobinostat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. Reduce the panobinostat starting dose to 10 mg if co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 56. Clarithromycin decreases the levels of pantothenic acid by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 57. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of parecoxib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 58. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of paricalcitol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 59. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of paromomycin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 60. Both clarithromycin and paroxetine prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 61. Both clarithromycin and pasireotide prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 62. Both clarithromycin and pazopanib prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 63. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of perampanel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 64. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of pimozide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely.
